rv.q: Rather, in a playful production by Anthony Banks, it is brisk and lightweight with enough of an edge to let the actors show a range that goes from sweet to sour.
Sadly, the play does not quite pull off the same balance elsewhere, despite the virtuoso performances.
This style might work as a radio play, but feels heavy-handed as a piece of theatre.
The Gap is a beautiful slice of real life, all wrapped up in a tapestry of Northern humour.

cn.t: Cartwright's nostalgic two-hander about reunited 1960s Soho friends divides critics, with some charmed by the stars' chemistry and audacious energy, while others find it shallow and heavy-handed in its metaphors.
